API authentication
All API requests require a valid access token.
Header format
The SDK and tester use the same authentication rules so you can reuse flows during local validation and integration debugging.
Authorization: Bearer <your-access-token>
Token types
Session Token: minted by the backend after the browser completes Privy login and used for the active web session.
Automation Token: created from Profile > Automation Access for CLI, CI, and agent workflows.
Service Account Token: machine identity token for tenant-scoped automation.
Token format
Uses the PASETO v4.local format, which is safer than JWT and supports symmetric encryption.
CLI onboarding

The CLI cannot complete Privy login directly and there is no username/password login endpoint. Sign in on the web first, issue a token from the Dashboard Tokens page, then configure that token in the CLI or your integration.

toani config init --url https://your-api.example.com --token <AUTOMATION_TO

SDK installation
Quick start for the Toani Vault TypeScript/JavaScript SDK
npm install @toani/vault-sdk
Copy

The SDK source lives at sdk-typescript/ in the project root and can be linked locally for development and testing. The package has been migrated from @credbridge/sdk to @toani/vault-sdk. The old package name is deprecated.

npm link ../../sdk-typescript
Basic example
Complete example for common operations
Copy
import { ToaniVaultSDK } from '@toani/vault-sdk';

// Initialize the SDK (Note: CredBridgeSDK is deprecated, please migrate to ToaniVaultSDK)
const sdk = new ToaniVaultSDK({
  baseUrl: 'http://localhost:8082',
  token: 'v4.local.your-token-here',
  timeout: 30000,
});

// 1. Create a username/password credential
const credential = await sdk.credentials.createUsernamePassword(
  'schwab',
  'user@example.com',
  'SecurePassword123!',
  { expiresAt: 1774000000 }
);

console.log('Created:', credential.credential_id);

// 2. List credentials
